podcast.body: This song, originally a hit for Roy Brown in 1947, was also released by Wynonie Harris, another Black performer. Both versions contributed significantly to embedding the idea of "rockin'" as a musical element into public awareness. "That same song was released by Winnone Harris, a black performer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Wynonie Harris's cover version of Roy Brown's song, this rendition became a world-changing hit in the R&B market, significantly outselling Brown's original. It features distinctive "hoi hoi" vocals, borrowed from "The Honeydripper," and an instrumental introduction based on "When the Saints Go Marching In," along with an added backbeat, leading many to consider it the first rock and roll record. "Not Roy Brown's original is the one that people call the first rock and roll record."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
